summary: [Digital Ethiopia 2030](2025-12-21 PM Abiy launches Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy) was launched in December 2025 on three pillars of access, equal opportunity and trust, and is the standing national strategy.
developments:
The strategy sets targets of 128m subscriptions and an identity for every adult by 2030, together with a sevenfold rise in digital payments ([Digital Ethiopia 2030](2026-01-27 Digital Ethiopia 2030 Charting a Sovereign Path to Prosperity)).

The council overseeing the programme restated in July 2026 that it is to be judged on lives changed rather than systems deployed, [a claim with no published measure behind it](2026-07-30-fana-deputy-pm-technology-must-improve-lives-digital-transformation-council).

No implementation plan, budget allocation against the pillars or progress report is held.

summary: The [Digital Government Strategy and Enterprise Architecture 2024-2029](2024-07-11 Ethiopia's Digital Government Strategy and Enterprise Architecture 2024-2029) has been in force since July 2024 with no revision on the record.
developments:
The strategy and its enterprise architecture were published in July 2024 and run to 2029, and remain the standing statement of how government systems are to be built ([the strategy](2024-07-11 Ethiopia's Digital Government Strategy and Enterprise Architecture 2024-2029)).

The base holds nothing on implementation against it: no progress report, no compliance review and no register of systems assessed against the architecture.

summary: A sovereign cloud and a forensic laboratory are [named in the national strategy](2025-12-21 PM Abiy launches Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy) as intentions, with no separate storage or cloud policy held.
developments:
December 2025's national strategy places a sovereign cloud and a forensic laboratory among the foundations it sets out ([Digital Ethiopia 2030](2025-12-21 PM Abiy launches Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy)).

No siting decision, procurement, operator or date exists for either facility, and no data storage or cloud strategy is held as a document in its own right.

summary: The [e-government interoperability framework](2024-07-19 Ethiopia's e-government leap to interoperability (EeGIF)) has been in development since July 2024 and the base records no completion.
developments:
The framework was published in July 2024 and is recorded as still in development two years on ([the framework](2024-07-19 Ethiopia's e-government leap to interoperability (EeGIF))).

No adopted version, compliance mandate or list of systems built to it is held, which is the gap the approved national data exchange platform would have to close.

summary: A [national artificial intelligence policy](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance) adopted in 2024 is in force, known to the base only at second hand.
developments:
The policy was adopted in 2024 and its existence reaches the base through a July 2026 account of the country joining a Shanghai-based cooperation body ([policy in force](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance)).

The policy text, its objectives, any implementation plan and any review are all absent, so what is recorded is that a policy exists and not what it says.

summary: A national data governance strategy is being drafted [around named use cases](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities) in health, agriculture and public financial management.
developments:
The strategy is being anchored in concrete use cases rather than written first and applied afterwards, with agriculture and public financial management the test domains alongside health ([use-case approach](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities)).

No draft text, adopting instrument or timetable is published, so the approach is on the record and the policy itself is not.

summary: [Proclamation 1321/2024](2024-08-30 Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321-2024 (overview)) has been in force since July 2024, a comprehensive regime with extraterritorial reach and no secondary directives behind it.
developments:
The proclamation took effect on 24 July 2024 as a comprehensive personal data regime reaching beyond the country's borders ([Proclamation 1321/2024](2024-08-30 Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321-2024 (overview))).

What the base does not hold is any instrument under it: the directives that would give the proclamation operative content were still unissued a year after commencement ([a year on](2025-11-15-ethiopia-data-protection-law-slow-enforcement)).

summary: The [communications authority](2024-08-30 Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321-2024 (overview)) is the designated regulator, and a year after commencement it had taken no enforcement action.
developments:
The proclamation names the Ethiopian Communications Authority as regulator rather than creating a dedicated body ([Proclamation 1321/2024](2024-08-30 Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321-2024 (overview))).

A year after commencement the authority had yet to enforce and public awareness was low, on a base where the national identity authenticates about 4m times a day across more than 150 agencies ([a year on](2025-11-15-ethiopia-data-protection-law-slow-enforcement)).

No budget, staffing figure, register of controllers or decision of any kind is held for the authority in its data-protection role.

summary: [Proclamation 1426/2026](2026-07-21-ethiopia-critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-proclamation-1426-2026) designates twelve critical sectors and places eighteen obligations on their owners and operators, commencing about July 2027.
developments:
The proclamation was signed at Addis Ababa on 21 July 2026, and article 28 sets commencement one year after gazettement ([Proclamation 1426/2026](2026-07-21-ethiopia-critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-proclamation-1426-2026)).

The designated sectors run from information and communications technology, financial services and transport to agriculture, trade and industry; a Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Fund is established, and the security agency is to write sector standards, give technical assistance and enforce through the transition ([briefing on the proclamation](2026-08-07-ethiopia-critical-infrastructure-cybersecurity-proclamation-insa)).

Ratification, assent and commencement dates are not established in the base, and the regulations the Council of Ministers and the agency may make under articles 26 and 27 do not yet exist.

progress: Mixed, the central bank widened a prohibition by notice while a court struck down a decree
summary: The central bank widened its [virtual-asset prohibition](2026-07-23-reporter-nbe-reaffirms-ban-virtual-assets) to the whole category, and a court [struck down a decree](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown) revoking licences without a court order.
developments:
A central-bank public notice of 23 July 2026 widened the prohibition by clarification rather than by new rule, covering use, purchase, sale, exchange, transfer, trading, settlement and facilitation absent express authorisation, with no new regulation and no enforcement mechanism announced ([public notice](2026-07-23-reporter-nbe-reaffirms-ban-virtual-assets)).

The Federal High Court of Lideta struck down a December 2025 lottery-administration decree that had cut banking services to betting platforms and gateways, holding revocation of a licence without a court order unconstitutional ([the ruling](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown)).

No payments proclamation or electronic transactions statute is held, so the operative law reaches the base as directives, notices and one judgment.

summary: No instrument compels agencies to integrate with the unified service platform, [on its own regional executives' account](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill).
developments:
Regional executives of the unified public-service platform say no legal framework obliges agencies to join it, so integration rests on agreement between them ([platform review](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill)).

The base holds no interoperability proclamation, no data-sharing regulation and no mandate under the e-government interoperability framework, which has itself been in development since 2024.

summary: A draft amendment would add [service provider duties, site blocking and take-down notices](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision) to the 2004 copyright proclamation, the first platform-liability instrument held.
developments:
The intellectual property authority reported in August 2026 that the amendment is being drafted after several consultation rounds, and would put duties on internet service providers, set procedures for blocking infringing sites and create a rights-holder take-down notice ([the authority's account](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision)).

Enforcement would stay rights-holder-initiated and by web address, because channel operators cannot be identified, against existing remedies of one-to-ten-year sentences and fines to 25,000 Birr ([the same report](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision)).

A draft proclamation ratifying accession to the Berne Convention is before the Council of Ministers, with no parliamentary date published ([the report again](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision)).

summary: The state development bank adopted a policy [classifying client credit information and four other categories as permanently non-disclosable](2026-08-08-dbe-client-credit-info-classified).
developments:
The policy, reported in August 2026, exempts client credit information, legal case files, strategy papers, security protocols and third-party contracts from declassification where disclosure could cause substantial harm to the bank, its stakeholders or the national interest, and lets the bank decline requests that would require it to create records it does not hold ([disclosure policy](2026-08-08-dbe-client-credit-info-classified)).

No instrument number, gazette reference or appeal mechanism is stated, and the base holds no general access-to-information statute against which to read it.

summary: No independent impact assessment, redress mechanism or statutory limit on state access to the identity system is held, [against 46.5m registrations](2026-08-09-ethiopia-fayda-digital-id-mass-profiling-critique).
developments:
A published critique argues the identity system risks becoming an instrument of mass profiling in the absence of independent data-protection impact assessments, meaningful citizen rights and legal limits on state access ([critique](2026-08-09-ethiopia-fayda-digital-id-mass-profiling-critique)).

In August 2026 the foreign ministry circulated a note asking every accredited diplomatic mission and international organisation to submit lists and addresses of all Ethiopian and foreign employees without diplomatic privileges, together with tenant and landlord details ([diplomatic note](2026-08-20-birrmetrics-mfa-missions-staff-property-records)).

No legal basis, retention rule, data controller or purpose limitation is stated in the note as reported.

The regulator now says the secondary law is coming: [four directives are expected to be approved in the coming months and a registration portal for data controllers and processors has been previewed](2025-11-15-ethiopia-data-protection-law-slow-enforcement), an early step towards a national register of them. The directives are unpublished, the portal was shown at a workshop co-hosted with a vendor, and a year after the proclamation took effect nothing has been enforced under it.

summary: Identity cooperation was agreed with [Zambia](2026-03-24 Zambia looking for MOSIP system integrator to support digital ID project) in March 2026, and a three-year [memorandum with Mozambique](2026-04-27-mozambique-ethiopia-mou-digital-identity-clubofmozambique) followed in April.
developments:
The Mozambique memorandum was signed at Addis Ababa on 27 April 2026 between Mozambique's digital transformation agency and the Ethiopian state digital-identity enterprise, and is extendable by consent ([memorandum](2026-04-27-mozambique-ethiopia-mou-digital-identity-clubofmozambique)).

Under it the Ethiopian side provides digital-identity, pilot, interoperability and joint-cybersecurity support, coordinated through a joint working group ([trade account](2026-04-28 Mozambique taps Ethiopia's digital ID expertise in DPI partnership)).

The Zambian arrangement is recorded only as identity cooperation agreed, with no text, term or scope on the record ([Zambia integrator search](2026-03-24 Zambia looking for MOSIP system integrator to support digital ID project)).

summary: A terrestrial corridor with Djibouti, Sudan and Saudi Arabia [entered active deployment](2026-08-20-tan-ethio-telecom-horizon-fibre-corridor) in August 2026, having become binding in February.
developments:
The December 2024 memorandum between the three national operators became a binding agreement in February 2026 ([binding agreement](2026-02-05-horizon-fiber-binding-agreement-connectingafrica)).

By August the end-to-end solution architecture was finalised and site-material procurement complete, with the stated route extended to Jeddah ([deployment](2026-08-20-tan-ethio-telecom-horizon-fibre-corridor)).

No route length, cost, in-service date or transit-revenue projection is published, so the transit-hub claim rests on the corridor's geography alone, and one of the four territories it crosses is at war.

summary: A bilateral health memorandum [provides for a data-sharing arrangement](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia) still to be negotiated, expected to run two years beyond its five-year term.
developments:
Clause 2.5.2 of the December 2025 memorandum has the two governments intending to negotiate an arrangement for exchanging data on long-term performance and for accountability to the United States Congress, and clause 4.7 makes failure to fulfil the specimen and data sharing arrangements grounds for changing or discontinuing assistance, although the memorandum creates no specimen arrangement ([memorandum](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia)).

A rights organisation reading the seven signed memoranda puts Ethiopia among five whose text requires unilateral sharing of specimens and pathogen-sequencing data, and all seven as requiring broad audit access ([assessment](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements)); no arrangement text is published, and a subset posted by the State Department in March 2026 was removed ([records complaint](2026-04-02-public-citizen-v-department-of-state-foia-complaint)).

summary: [National livestock data standards](2026-07-29-devgateway-ethiopia-livestock-information-system-dpi) were endorsed in July 2026 and cascaded through training of trainers to more than 300 experts and collectors.
developments:
The standards were developed with the agriculture ministry, endorsed, and then cascaded on a training-of-trainers model ([livestock data standards](2026-07-29-devgateway-ethiopia-livestock-information-system-dpi)).

They underpin a livestock information system drawing on five priority databases, which repositions animal identification from an export tool to a national asset register and links it to disease surveillance and vaccination records ([the same account](2026-07-29-devgateway-ethiopia-livestock-information-system-dpi)).

The account is the implementing organisation's own, after four years with a team embedded in the ministry, and is uncorroborated in the base.

summary: The national identity is built on [an open-source international platform](2026-07-07 Beyond the Platform Understanding the Growing MOSIP Ecosystem) and is the reference deployment other implementations point to.
developments:
The platform is modular open source under the Mozilla Public Licence, incubated at a research institute in Bangalore, and the Ethiopian deployment is its flagship ([platform account](2026-07-07 Beyond the Platform Understanding the Growing MOSIP Ecosystem)).

That adoption is the base's clearest evidence of an international standard taken up, and its only one: no conformity assessment, standards-body membership or certification against international instruments is on the record.

summary: A civil-society [project on climate disinformation](2026-08-19-cipesa-unesco-climate-information-integrity) launched in August 2026 will track government communications ahead of the November climate conference.
developments:
The project covers Uganda and Ethiopia under a wider international initiative, and combines research mapping how climate disinformation spreads and who drives it with a fact-checking masterclass at the 2026 internet-freedom forum and online training for journalists and civil society ([project launch](2026-08-19-cipesa-unesco-climate-information-integrity)).

No budget or duration is stated, and the base holds no other instance of non-governmental input to national digital policy: no consultation record, no submission and no published response to one.

summary: Public argument over telecommunications reform [has moved from whether to liberalise to whether the state is provider or regulator](2026-01-10-beyond-connectivity-ethiopia-digital-future-reform-reporter).
developments:
The monopoly ended in 2021 with one new full licensee since, and the published debate now turns on whether the state should act as provider or as regulator and partner ([reform commentary](2026-01-10-beyond-connectivity-ethiopia-digital-future-reform-reporter)).

That is the only held instance of open policy argument, and it is a newspaper commentary rather than a consultation, a hearing record or a government response to either.

progress: Advanced, mostly the birr float rather than real growth
summary: Digital lines in the federal budget rose to [ETB 9.05bn for FY2026/27](2026-07-07-eth-2026-144) from ETB 3.75bn, dominated by a single university project.
developments:
Thirty-four digital budget lines run across three years: ETB 1.21bn appropriated in FY2024/25 against an outturn of ETB 1.53bn, ETB 3.75bn in FY2025/26 and ETB 9.05bn in FY2026/27, the last dominated by an artificial-intelligence university line ([budget lines](2026-07-07-eth-2026-144)).

They sit inside a federal budget of 2.34 trillion birr for FY2026/27, ratified in July 2026 and up 21.3% on the year before ([budget ratified](2026-07-07-eth-fana-parliament-ratifies-2-34tn-birr-budget-efy2019)).

Execution is now published: the mid-year review for 2025/26 records ETB 704.7bn mobilised, 48.1% of the annual target, against ETB 798.2bn spent, 48.3% of the approved budget, with recurrent spending at 39.3% of its budget against 62.9% of capital ([mid-year review](2026-04-01-ethiopia-mid-year-budget-implementation-review-2025-26)).

summary: The second network operator is [funded to about US$2.67bn](2026-07-30-safaricom-ethiopia-funding-ifc-standard-bank), and a change of control over it completed in June 2026.
developments:
The parent's disclosure at 30 June 2026 puts funding of the Ethiopian operator at KES 345.7bn, about US$2.672bn: KES 298.3bn of equity and KES 47.3bn of debt from a commercial bank and the International Finance Corporation, including the US$850m licence fee and the US$150m mobile-money fee ([funding disclosure](2026-07-30-safaricom-ethiopia-funding-ifc-standard-bank)).

A funding round restricted to one shareholder family lifted the lead holding to 54.1% in March 2026 from 51.67%, cutting the two development financiers to 9.5% and 6.81% with a right to reacquire what they lost ([the same disclosure](2026-07-30-safaricom-ethiopia-funding-ifc-standard-bank)).

The incumbent's 10% public share offer closed in February 2025, distributed through its wallet ([public offer](2025-01-11-ethio-telecom-extends-public-offering-deadline-reporter)), and the change of control completed on 30 June 2026 ([completion](2026-07-27-vodacom-548-billion-mobile-money-q1-fy2027)).

summary: The [US$350m identity credit](2023-11-20 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - project appraisal document) is rated satisfactory on both counts and 23% disbursed, and a small extension grant was committed in July 2026.
developments:
The identity project is an SDR 228.2m credit of US$300m plus an SDR 38.1m grant of US$50m from the window for host communities and refugees ([appraisal](2023-11-20 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - project appraisal document)).

The March 2026 implementation support mission rated it satisfactory on development objective and on implementation progress, with 23% disbursed and US$46.4m disbursed since the start of the 2026 financial year ([aide-memoire](2026-05-18 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - implementation support mission aide-memoire)).

A US$300,000 grant committed in July 2026 converts a catalytic start-up initiative into a programme delivering agricultural extension through digital channels to 2028 ([extension grant](2026-07-31-iati-xm-dac-41301-763888-ethiopia-digital-extension-services)).

summary: The incumbent reports [99.8% population coverage](2026-04-20-ethio-telecom-99-8-coverage-smart-infrastructure-techafricanews) on about 90m subscribers, and the second operator 14.7m active customers.
developments:
Mobile connections reached 93.2m in late 2025, 68.4% of the population, from 85.4m and 63.8% in early 2025 ([connections](2025-11-08 Digital 2026 Ethiopia (DataReportal))).

The incumbent reported 99.8% population coverage in April 2026 ([coverage](2026-04-20-ethio-telecom-99-8-coverage-smart-infrastructure-techafricanews)), and the second operator 14.7m ninety-day active customers in August after upgrading more than 67 sites across nine southern towns against congestion and power problems ([site upgrades](2026-08-20-safaricom-ethiopia-upgrades-67-sites)).

Contracts signed at the 2026 industry congress cover 1,500 new sites and 502 upgrades from one vendor and 647 from another, under a three-year corporate strategy to 2028 ([expansion contracts](2026-03-09-ethio-telecom-network-expansion-mwc-barcelona-addisstandard), [strategy](2025-08-26-ethiotelecom-next-horizon-digital-beyond-2028-strategy)); a review in August put 879 sites complete under the second programme ([progress review](2026-08-10-ethio-telecom-zte-network-modernisation-4g-coverage-92-percent)).

summary: Data and internet became the incumbent's largest revenue line in the year to June 2026, at [31.1% against mobile voice at 23.5%](2026-08-01-ethiopia-data-overtakes-voice-ethio-telecom).
developments:
It was the first financial year in which data and internet, not mobile voice, were the largest share of the incumbent's revenue ([data overtakes voice](2026-08-01-ethiopia-data-overtakes-voice-ethio-telecom)).

Total revenue was 215.8bn birr with operating profit of 92.9bn birr, on the operator's own unaudited figures ([results](2026-07-23-fana-ethio-telecom-215-8-billion-birr-revenue-telebirr)).

A streaming service and a zero-touch broadband product launched in February 2026 ([new services](2026-02-23-ethio-telecom-telestream-zero-touch-broadband-techafricanews)).

No independent measure of internet use is held: the base carries revenue mix and connection counts, not a survey of users.

summary: The second operator [began building fibre](2025-08-02-safaricom-ethiopia-begins-fibre-deployment-reporter) from Afdera to Mekelle in August 2025, the only backbone construction the base holds.
developments:
Construction on that route started in August 2025 and is the only record of national fibre being built by anyone other than the incumbent ([fibre deployment](2025-08-02-safaricom-ethiopia-begins-fibre-deployment-reporter)).

No route length, capacity, cost or completion date is published, and the base holds no figure at all for the national backbone's route kilometres, its utilisation or its redundancy.

summary: A multi-terabit corridor to [Jeddah through Djibouti and Sudan](2026-08-20-tan-ethio-telecom-horizon-fibre-corridor) entered deployment, the first new international route the base holds.
developments:
The corridor is described as multi-terabit and now runs to Saudi Arabia, which would give a landlocked country a second path to international capacity alongside its existing transit ([corridor deployment](2026-08-20-tan-ethio-telecom-horizon-fibre-corridor)).

No capacity figure, in-service date or price is published, and the base holds no measurement of international bandwidth in use, per person or in total, against which to read it.

summary: Satellite services are licensable as a [class landing-right authorisation](2021-07-01-eca-telecommunications-licensing-directive-792-2021), and no low-earth-orbit operator is authorised on the record.
developments:
The licensing directive of July 2021 carries a class authorisation for satellite voice, internet and data services provided without infrastructure or a network facility in the country, one of thirteen class licences alongside internet service provider, data centre, hosting and terminal authorisations ([licensing directive](2021-07-01-eca-telecommunications-licensing-directive-792-2021)).

There is no orbit-specific determination and no authorised operator on record, and the regulator denied in July 2025 that any discussions with a low-earth-orbit operator had taken place ([the same record](2021-07-01-eca-telecommunications-licensing-directive-792-2021)).

progress: No change, a first mention with no capacity figure behind it
summary: The country is [named among markets diversifying Africa's estate](2026-07-28-africa-data-centre-capacity-500mw-890mw-pipeline), with no capacity figure of its own on the record.
developments:
A July 2026 survey of African capacity names Ethiopia alongside Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco as markets diversifying an estate in which South Africa holds more than 60% of operational capacity ([capacity survey](2026-07-28-africa-data-centre-capacity-500mw-890mw-pipeline)).

No megawatt figure, facility count or pipeline is given for Ethiopia itself, so the base records that the country is on the list and nothing about where on it.

summary: An in-country [cloud exchange](2026-04-01 Wingu Africa debuts cloud exchange platform in Ethiopia) went live in April 2026, selling compute, Kubernetes and storage priced in birr and hybrid with two global clouds.
developments:
The platform offers compute, Kubernetes, drive and security services priced in local currency and interoperating with two global cloud providers, and its operator frames it as compliance with local data rules ([cloud exchange](2026-04-01 Wingu Africa debuts cloud exchange platform in Ethiopia)).

No capacity, customer count or price list is published, and the base holds no other nationally operated cloud or data centre, so this is the whole of the domestic-provider record.

summary: A [40 MW bitcoin-mining site](2026-01-12 Bitdeer completes 40 MW Oromia bitcoin-mining site in Ethiopia) was completed in January 2026 with 20 MW more in progress, drawn by cheap electricity.
developments:
The operator completed 40 MW at the Oromia site with a further 20 MW under construction, having weighed Nigeria for the same project before relocating it on far cheaper electricity ([mining site](2026-01-12 Bitdeer completes 40 MW Oromia bitcoin-mining site in Ethiopia)).

The load is a mining site rather than a data centre serving domestic compute, and the base holds nothing on water, on grid capacity reserved for such loads, or on the tariff the electricity is sold at.

summary: Diesel generator running time across the incumbent's network is [down by up to 40%](2026-08-04-ethio-telecom-green-legacy-solar-infrastructure) on hybrid solar and battery installations.
developments:
The operator reports 867 hybrid solar-and-battery systems and 1,114 lithium-ion storage units across its network, cutting diesel generator running time by up to 40% ([green operator](2026-08-04-ethio-telecom-green-legacy-solar-infrastructure)).

The figures are the operator's own and unaudited, and they measure a network's dependence on its own backup rather than the grid itself: no outage statistics, interruption indices or utility disclosure are held.

progress: Mixed, solar at network sites is rising while rural electricity behind the community health system stays at 9%
summary: Solar on the incumbent's network reached 39.72 MW, against rural electricity reaching [9% of community health workers](2023-06-07 Barriers, facilitators and motivators of electronic community health information system use among health workers in Ethiopia).
developments:
Installed solar across the incumbent's network stood at 39.72 MW in August 2026, up 12.72 MW over the financial year, on 190 fully solar-powered sites serving rural and off-grid communities ([green operator](2026-08-04-ethio-telecom-green-legacy-solar-infrastructure)).

Behind that, the community health information system is offline-first by necessity because rural electricity reaches 9% of its users and fourth-generation coverage 4%, and the ministry distributed about 29,950 power banks with its tablets ([community health system](2023-06-07 Barriers, facilitators and motivators of electronic community health information system use among health workers in Ethiopia)).

progress: Mixed, services are being added to the unified platform ahead of the systems behind them
summary: Services are onboarded to the unified platform [before the underlying systems are digitised](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill), on two incompatible integration models.
developments:
The platform's own regional executives say services are being onboarded ahead of the digitisation of the systems that would serve them, and that two incompatible integration models have emerged as a result ([platform review](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill)).

The base holds no inventory of government hardware or software, no uptime figure for any government system and no assessment of the estate, so the platform's own account is the only evidence on the question.

progress: Mixed, the national health information system held on local staffing while donor-funded surveillance stopped
summary: The national health information system [stayed online on local staffing](2026-05-26 A Year After USAID Reclaiming Control of Data Systems – Development Gateway An IREX Venture – Data and digital solutions for international development) after the 2025 aid freeze, while donor-funded livestock and zoonotic surveillance was suspended.
developments:
The 2025 United States aid freeze suspended livestock and zoonotic surveillance, while the national health information system continued to run on local staffing, which is the argument its implementers draw for locally owned routine systems ([a year after the freeze](2026-05-26 A Year After USAID Reclaiming Control of Data Systems – Development Gateway An IREX Venture – Data and digital solutions for international development)).

The contrast is the only direct evidence held on national capacity to keep government systems running, and it covers one sector: no civil-service skills audit, vacancy figure or maintenance contract register is on file.

summary: Cybersecurity foundations are [named in the national strategy](2025-12-21 PM Abiy launches Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy), and the dominant state bank is [moving to a zero-trust architecture](2026-08-16-capitalethiopia-ai-cyber-threats-financial-sector).
developments:
The December 2025 strategy makes the security agency's cybersecurity work one of the foundations of the national programme ([Digital Ethiopia 2030](2025-12-21 PM Abiy launches Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy)).

The dominant state bank reported in August 2026 that it is moving its information-systems architecture to a zero-trust model supported by artificial intelligence ([financial sector threats](2026-08-16-capitalethiopia-ai-cyber-threats-financial-sector)).

No national readiness assessment, incident statistics, emergency response team disclosure or sectoral audit is held, so the record is a stated intention and one institution's own account.

summary: A national data exchange platform was [approved by a prime-ministerial board](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill) in July 2026, paired with a predictive model and not yet built.
developments:
The board approved the platform alongside an artificial-intelligence predictive model, at the same meeting that was diagnosing the absence of an interoperability layer ([board approval](2026-07-25-birrmetrics-mesob-meets-the-monster-it-was-built-to-kill)).

Nothing is published on architecture, budget, timetable or operator, and the interoperability framework that would govern such a platform has itself been in development since 2024, so approval is the whole of the position.

summary: The identity has been [integrated with tax administration](2025-07-12 How Fayda powers Ethiopia's MESOB one-stop government platform) since December 2023 and was [made mandatory for schooling](2025-11-12 Fayda passes 28 million registrations; education mandate) in November 2025.
developments:
Tax administration was integrated with the national identity in December 2023 and the base records no change since ([tax integration](2025-07-12 How Fayda powers Ethiopia's MESOB one-stop government platform)).

The mandate of November 2025 requires the identity for school enrolment and for sitting examinations ([education mandate](2025-11-12 Fayda passes 28 million registrations; education mandate)).

Neither integration is described in technical terms: there is no statement of what is exchanged, under what authority, or whether the exchange runs through a shared layer or point to point.

summary: Health is the most fragmented sector on the record, at [more than 70 siloed platforms and 200 pilots](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities), converging on one record-interoperability pilot.
developments:
Work on the data governance strategy surfaced health as the most fragmented sector, holding more than 70 siloed platforms and more than 200 pilots, and it is converging on a multi-tenant electronic medical record interoperability pilot ([use cases](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities)).

The pilot has no published scope, participating facilities or date, and the base holds no health information exchange, no terminology standard and no patient identifier arrangement.

summary: The programme [adopted an open external assessment framework](2026-05-12 Strengthening Fayda Ethiopia's improvement journey through the Digital ID Assessment) as its official monitoring instrument and re-ran it in May 2026.
developments:
The assessment was first run in early 2025 and re-run in May 2026, and the identity programme has adopted it as its official monitoring instrument rather than commissioning its own ([assessment](2026-05-12 Strengthening Fayda Ethiopia's improvement journey through the Digital ID Assessment)).

The scores, findings and any remediation plan are not held, so the base records that the system is being measured and not what the measurement says.

The deployment is the flagship implementation of the platform it is built on, which other national programmes take as their reference ([platform account](2026-07-07 Beyond the Platform Understanding the Growing MOSIP Ecosystem)).

summary: Enrolment reached [49.1m by August 2026](2026-08-24-fayda-digital-id-49-1m-enrolments-ethiopia-biometricupdate) from 16.4m in June 2025, on 12,000 registration kits, against a 90m target.
developments:
Enrolments stood at 49.1m on 24 August 2026, from about 46.5m in July and 16.4m in June 2025, on 12,000 biometric registration kits deployed nationally ([enrolment count](2026-08-24-fayda-digital-id-49-1m-enrolments-ethiopia-biometricupdate)).

The incumbent operator accounts for 69% of all registrations, about 32m people since April 2024, of which 20.19m in the year to June 2026, with 9.35m cards printed against about 9.4m ordered ([operator channel](2026-07-24-ena-ethio-telecom-69-percent-fayda-digital-id-enrollees)).

The second operator took two lots of the registration project in July 2026, covering Afar, Amhara, Tigray, Sidama and three southern regions ([registration lots](2026-07-06 Safaricom Ethiopia partners National ID Program to expand digital identity registration)), and a four-lot procurement of about US$54m for registration super agents awaits the lender's clearance ([aide-memoire](2026-05-18 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - implementation support mission aide-memoire)).

summary: The identity programme was [incorporated as a state-owned enterprise](2026-08-05-faydaverse-ethiopia-dpi-soe) in August 2026 under the sovereign wealth fund, and plans to widen its wallet.
developments:
The programme was commercialised into the sovereign wealth fund with a 10bn birr cap in March 2026 ([wealth fund](2026-03-13-fayda-joins-sovereign-wealth-fund-1m-weekly-biometricupdate)), then incorporated as a state-owned enterprise on 4 August 2026 with the programme's executive director appointed chief executive ([enterprise](2026-08-05-faydaverse-ethiopia-dpi-soe)).

The holding company states the purpose as attracting partnerships and creating long-term value, and positions the enterprise for export ([the same account](2026-08-05-faydaverse-ethiopia-dpi-soe)).

The wallet is planned to carry academic transcripts, professional licences, healthcare records, property titles and compliance data beyond the government credentials it holds today, with no timetable, consent model, controller arrangement or regulatory approval stated ([wallet expansion](2026-08-08-ethiopia-fayda-faydaverse-digital-wallet-expansion)).

summary: [194m identity verifications](2026-08-24-fayda-digital-id-49-1m-enrolments-ethiopia-biometricupdate) have been performed across 150 integrated agencies, and biometric kits have gone to banks.
developments:
The programme reports 194m electronic know-your-customer verifications to date across 150 integrated agencies, on its own unaudited figures ([verification count](2026-08-24-fayda-digital-id-49-1m-enrolments-ethiopia-biometricupdate)).

Two thousand portable face, fingerprint and iris kits were distributed to 31 banks in November 2025 of 6,000 planned, at about US$17m, with the remaining 4,000 under a re-issued tender ([biometric kits](2025-11-11-ethiopia-banks-receive-biometric-kits-fayda-biometricupdate)).

No authentication failure rate, exception-handling procedure or availability figure is published.

summary: All bank accounts were [required to be harmonised with the identity](2025-12-10 NBE launches full integration of Fayda digital ID with the banking system) by March 2026, and one bank now [opens accounts on it alone](2026-04-07-dashen-bank-first-digital-id-accounts-biometricupdate).
developments:
The December 2025 directive required every bank account to be harmonised with the national identity by 30 March 2026 ([banking integration](2025-12-10 NBE launches full integration of Fayda digital ID with the banking system)).

A commercial bank opened the first accounts on the identity alone in April 2026, without other documents ([remote account opening](2026-04-07-dashen-bank-first-digital-id-accounts-biometricupdate)).

Nothing is held on compliance with the deadline: no share of accounts harmonised, no extension and no enforcement action is on the record.

summary: The central bank published a [five-year payments strategy](2025-12-09 Ethiopia launches National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030) in December 2025 and directed the banking system to harmonise accounts with the national identity.
developments:
The strategy for 2026 to 2030 was published against 18.5tn birr a year in digital transactions ([payments strategy](2025-12-09 Ethiopia launches National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030)).

The following day the bank set a March 2026 deadline for full integration of the national identity with the banking system ([banking integration](2025-12-10 NBE launches full integration of Fayda digital ID with the banking system)).

The bank's supervisory record is thinner than its strategy: no licensing register, supervisory report or consumer-complaint statistics are held.

summary: A mobile wallet began [collecting regional tax](2026-07-28-m-pesa-ethiopia-launches-digital-tax-payment-service-for-amhara-region) in July 2026, described as the first of a planned series with regional revenue authorities.
developments:
The service went live with one regional revenue authority in July 2026 ([regional tax payment](2026-07-28-m-pesa-ethiopia-launches-digital-tax-payment-service-for-amhara-region)).

No collection volume, taxpayer count or fee arrangement is published, and the base holds nothing on federal revenue collected through digital channels, which is the larger question.

summary: The incumbent's wallet reports [60.6m users and 4.19tn birr transacted](2026-07-23-fana-ethio-telecom-215-8-billion-birr-revenue-telebirr) in the year to June 2026, against 2.58m monthly active users on the challenger.
developments:
The incumbent's wallet moved 4.19tn birr in the year to June 2026, about 11bn birr a day, across 60.6m users, 410,700 agents and 440,100 merchants, with 21.64m customers on digital credit and microfinance ([wallet results](2026-07-23-fana-ethio-telecom-215-8-billion-birr-revenue-telebirr)).

The challenger reports monthly active users doubled to 2.58m in the quarter to June 2026 and registered merchants up 147.7% to 89,877, while mobile money is about 2% of the unit's service revenue against 45.6% in Kenya ([quarterly results](2026-08-03-safaricoms-ethiopian-unit-delivers-rapid-growth-but-mobile-money-struggles)); the base also holds 5.2m active users for the quarter to December 2025, and the two counts are not reconciled ([earlier count](2026-03-30 M-PESA Ethiopia surges 258% as EthSwitch fuels growth)).

The dominant state bank reports 3.48 billion digital transactions worth more than 22 trillion birr in 2025/26, which it puts at about 70 per cent of national digital transaction value ([bank figures](2026-08-16-capitalethiopia-ai-cyber-threats-financial-sector)).

The Global Findex 2025 reading puts [account ownership at 49 per cent of adults in 2024, up three points from 46 per cent in 2021](2025-07-23-findex-2025-ethiopia-digital-financial-leap), against more than 200 million digital accounts opened over the period, with financial literacy, limited smartphone access and physical distance named as what still excludes. Accounts opened and adults included move in opposite directions and nothing reconciles the two.

summary: The national health information system covers [more than 95% of facilities](2024-07-26 Maturity Assessment of District Health Information System Version 2 Implementation in Ethiopia Current Status and Improvement Pathways) at an assessed maturity of 2.81 of 5, weakest on infrastructure.
developments:
The district health information system has been national since 2018 and reaches more than 95% of facilities, at a maturity of 2.81 out of 5 with information and communications infrastructure weakest at 2.14 ([maturity assessment](2024-07-26 Maturity Assessment of District Health Information System Version 2 Implementation in Ethiopia Current Status and Improvement Pathways)).

Functionality for comparing reports received against reports expected was available in 75.0% of the data offices assessed in a four-country study run between November 2022 and July 2024 ([newborn data functionality](2025-12-01-impulse-erhis-newborn-data-functionalities)).

The community system reaches about 40,000 health extension workers ([community health system](2023-06-07 Barriers, facilitators and motivators of electronic community health information system use among health workers in Ethiopia)), and a case-management system used by 950 community health workers reports data-access time down from a month to a day ([case management](2026-08-10-ethiopia-digital-health-hiv-case-management-user-centered)).

A bilateral memorandum allocates US$18,850,149 to health data systems across 2026 to 2030, with Ethiopia carrying licensing, cloud, hardware and maintenance costs ([memorandum](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia)).

The pharmaceuticals supply service reports a modernised and digitalised supply chain, recognised with a continental award in August 2026 ([report](2026-08-26-ena-epss-pharmaceutical-supply-chain-digitalisation)).

summary: A revenue audit rested on [data conflating gateway throughput with gateway revenue](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown), restating one firm's three-year volume more than fourfold.
developments:
Data compiled for a revenue audit conflated gross transaction volume with gateway revenue, restating one gateway's three-year throughput of ETB 32bn as ETB 143.9bn and taxing the difference at 30% ([tax assessment](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown)).

Corrected datasets issued in April 2026 were not accepted, and ETB 818m was swept from frozen accounts in May against a liability counsel puts at ETB 20-30m, with parallel sweeps against two other gateways ([the same account](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown)).

The overstatement exceeds ETB 111bn, against a gateway commission of about 2.5% split with the state operator ([the account again](2026-07-25-reporter-economic-execution-ethiopia-fintechs-tax-crackdown)).

An international diagnostic of February 2025, across nine performance outcome areas, found the absence of a robust integrated tax administration information system adversely affecting the integrity of the registered taxpayer base, with online registration and updating of taxpayer details sought, electronic payment facilities not in place, and the use of electronic filing carried as an indicator in its own right ([diagnostic](2025-02-01-ethiopia-tadat-performance-assessment-2025)).

It is the only independent assessment of the administration's systems the base holds, and it predates the audit recorded above. An administration assessed as lacking an integrated system, and then producing a revenue assessment that conflated throughput with revenue, is one account read against the other.

summary: The unified platform's own catalogue lists [more than 180 services from 23 organisations](2026-08-23-mesob-centre-service-catalogue), against 41 services and 12 agencies a year earlier.
developments:
The public catalogue, read in August 2026, states more than 180 government services from 23 named provider organisations, each listed with required documents, processing time and fees ([service catalogue](2026-08-23-mesob-centre-service-catalogue)).

A government communication of April 2026 claims 2,260 services integrated, two months before the 185 stated at the June launch, so the two counts run concurrently on different bases rather than showing a rise ([government communication](2026-04-20-gcs-ethiopia-key-achievements-digital-sector-reform), [platform launch](2026-06-20 Ethiopia launches unified MESOB Platform to accelerate national digital transformation)).

Electronic government procurement is credited by the Auditor General with the decline in cash shortages across 163 audited federal institutions, in a report that also finds billions of Birr uncollected ([audit report](2026-07-06-ofag-annual-audit-report-efy-2017-presented)).

An unmanned police station opened in March 2026 with self-service kiosks for reports, fines and document requests ([police station](2026-03-22 Ethiopia opens Africa's first unmanned Smart Police Station)).

The transport and logistics ministry launched three national systems with the incumbent operator: a [cross-country public transport service system, an integrated fuel supply system and a national traffic point-based penalty management system](2025-01-01-ethiopia-nationwide-digital-transport-fuel-traffic-systems). A trade magazine account of the launch is the record; no coverage, volume or data-handling rule for a penalty system keyed to drivers is published.

summary: The capital reports [11 one-stop digital service centres](2026-07-20-amn-addis-mesob-digital-one-stop-service-centres) carrying more than 150 services from more than 25 integrated institutions.
developments:
At the close of the 2025/26 financial year the city administration reported 11 centres offering more than 150 services drawn from more than 25 integrated institutions ([one-stop centres](2026-07-20-amn-addis-mesob-digital-one-stop-service-centres)).

The figures are the operator's own, given by the centre's director general to the city administration's own media network, with no transaction volumes, users served, cost, uptime or independent evaluation published, and the base holds nothing at all on any other subnational tier.

summary: The [state artificial intelligence institute](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance), established in 2020, built the unified service platform and anchors the state's capability claim.
developments:
The institute has operated since 2020 and is credited with building the unified public-service platform, which is the state's principal claim to applied artificial intelligence capability ([the institute](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance)).

Nothing else is held: no inventory of models in government use, no procurement, no evaluation of any deployed system and no policy on automated decision-making within administration.

summary: Generative artificial intelligence services are [sold as bundles through a mobile wallet](2026-07-22-mpesa-ethiopia-gebeya-ai-mini-app), and no nationally developed model is held.
developments:
Bundles for generative application, website, game, video and music creation went on sale in July 2026 through the challenger's wallet, bought with mobile money and redeemed by voucher ([service bundles](2026-07-22-mpesa-ethiopia-gebeya-ai-mini-app)).

The base holds no nationally or regionally developed model, no training dataset, no compute facility and no research output, so what is recorded is the distribution of services built elsewhere.

progress: No change, two firms named and no output measured
summary: The base names [one domestic engineering firm](2026-07-28-nebyu-zekariyas-zewde-mareb-technologies) and [one foreign entrant with a local partner](2026-08-17-sybrin-ethiopia-digital-payments-modernisation), with no measure of national production.
developments:
An Addis Ababa engineering services firm founded in 2021 is the only named domestic producer on the record ([engineering firm](2026-07-28-nebyu-zekariyas-zewde-mareb-technologies)).

A South African financial-technology firm entered the payments market in August 2026 with a local engineering partner, aligning onboarding, fraud-management and workflow-automation tools with the national payments strategy, with no commitment value, customer or deployment date disclosed ([market entry](2026-08-17-sybrin-ethiopia-digital-payments-modernisation)).

No industry survey, employment figure, export value or firm count is held.

summary: An [artificial intelligence innovation pod](2026-02-19 Ethiopia launches AI UniPod to drive innovation) opened in February 2026, run with a development agency and the national university.
developments:
The pod opened in February 2026 with the United Nations Development Programme and Addis Ababa University ([innovation pod](2026-02-19 Ethiopia launches AI UniPod to drive innovation)).

It is the only hub the base holds: no incubator count, membership figure, funding total or record of what has come out of it is on file.

summary: [ETB 5bn was appropriated](2026-07-07-eth-2026-144) in the FY2026/27 budget to build an artificial intelligence university, with no site or timetable published.
developments:
The appropriation is ETB 5,000,000,000, carried as a single named capital project in the federal budget ratified in July 2026 ([budget line](2026-07-07-eth-2026-144), [budget ratified](2026-07-07-eth-fana-parliament-ratifies-2-34tn-birr-budget-efy2019)).

Nothing is published on site, design, intake, faculty or opening date, and the base holds no enrolment figure, graduate count or course inventory for any digital qualification at any existing institution.

summary: A [university law school is drafting](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision) the online-infringement amendment with the intellectual property authority.
developments:
The amendment to the copyright proclamation is being drafted with the Addis Ababa University School of Law after several rounds of consultation ([drafting](2026-08-01-ethiopia-eipa-online-copyright-infringement-law-revision)).

That is the whole of the record: no think tank, research centre or academic department is otherwise named as contributing to digital policy, and no commissioned research, submission or advisory appointment is held.

progress: No change, a first measurement with no earlier figure behind it
summary: The rural mobile-internet gender gap is put at [81%, against 29% in urban areas](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities).
developments:
The gap between men's and women's mobile internet use is reported at 81% in rural areas against 29% urban ([gender gap](2026-03-04 Ethiopia's approach to use cases shows how to ground data governance in real-world priorities)).

No earlier figure is held, so the level is on the record and the direction is not, and nothing is held on what is being done about it: no target, no programme and no gender-disaggregated figure for identity enrolment, account ownership or device access.

summary: A [refugee-inclusion framework](2026-07-16-fayda-refugee-inclusion-makatet-strategy-biometricupdate) covering 1.1m refugees and 2m displaced people makes the national identity central to a state-led model.
developments:
The framework adopted in July 2026 puts the national identity at the centre of a state-led inclusion model covering 1.1m refugees and 2m internally displaced people ([inclusion framework](2026-07-16-fayda-refugee-inclusion-makatet-strategy-biometricupdate)).

The lender's March 2026 mission records about 190,000 refugee registrations against 170,000 identity issuances ([aide-memoire](2026-05-18 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - implementation support mission aide-memoire)).

Neither figure is broken down by camp, region or status, and the base holds nothing on what services a refugee holding the identity can actually reach.

summary: A [1.5% revenue levy](2026-03-01-telecom-tax-universal-access-fund-reporter) funds universal access, and [handset financing](2026-07-17-ethio-telecom-huawei-digital-infrastructure) targets up to two million smartphones a year.
developments:
From March 2026 both operators contribute 1.5% of revenue to a universal access fund, about 2.5bn birr a year ([access fund levy](2026-03-01-telecom-tax-universal-access-fund-reporter)).

Financing deals with two banks target up to two million handsets a year for low-income customers on long-term instalments ([handset financing](2026-07-17-ethio-telecom-huawei-digital-infrastructure)).

A telco-agnostic wallet launched in December 2025 works on a subscriber module from any network and is verified against the national identity, removing network lock-in ([the wallet](2025-12-02-mpesa-lehulum-telco-agnostic-platform-connectingafrica)).

Nothing is published on what the access fund has disbursed, on how many handsets have been financed, or on the gap either is meant to close.

summary: A [United States health memorandum](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia) signed in December 2025 plans US$1,016,000,000 of support to 2030 against Ethiopia's US$450,000,000.
developments:
The memorandum covers activities from April 2026 to December 2030, states at clause 6.9 that it is not an international agreement, and was signed on the Ethiopian side by the Minister of Finance ([memorandum](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia)).

The United States reserves 6% of the top-line budget for its own management and operations ([the same text](2025-12-23-afghs-mou-ethiopia)).

It is the only United States or hyperscaler engagement held: no cloud provider agreement, technology company memorandum or bilateral digital instrument is on file.

summary: The country is a [founding member of a Shanghai-based artificial intelligence body](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance) and opened vendor tracks on cloud and data centres in July 2026.
developments:
Ethiopia is one of 29 founding states of the organisation, announced with 5,000 Chinese-funded training places over five years and support for joint open-source model development ([founding membership](2026-07-20-ethiopia-joins-waico-global-ai-alliance)). The constitutive text, membership list, powers, funding, voting rules and whether the agreement binds are all unestablished.

The incumbent operator opened scoping discussions with its radio-network vendor covering cloud, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data-centre services and wallet integration, with no value or term disclosed ([vendor scoping](2026-07-17-ethio-telecom-huawei-digital-infrastructure)), and a separate data-centre track with a Chinese manufacturer, with no site or value stated ([data-centre track](2026-07-16-ethio-telecom-inspur-partnership-techafricanews)).

One Chinese model accounts for about 20% of chatbot use in the country, the top of its African range ([model adoption](2026-03-12 China's DeepSeek gives US tech giants a run for their money as Microsoft and others expand AI push in Africa)).

summary: An Indian state rail telecom company [announced a data centre build](2026-01-09 RailTel to build Data Centre in Ethiopia (press release)) in January 2026, with nothing published since.
developments:
The announcement is a press release from the Indian company stating an intention to build a data centre ([announcement](2026-01-09 RailTel to build Data Centre in Ethiopia (press release))).

No site, capacity, value, partner, timetable or Ethiopian counterparty is named, and the base holds no other Indian engagement, so the record is one press release and its silence since.

summary: The 2023 identification proclamation became a binding operational requirement across banking, with migration to the new verification service mandated ([decision](2025-12-10-nbe-banks-verifayda-2-migration)).
developments:
The central bank and the national identity programme began harmonising all bank customer account numbers with the national digital identity, mandating migration from the first to the second verification service for all new and existing accounts with a deadline of 30 March 2026 ([decision](2025-12-10-nbe-banks-verifayda-2-migration)).

The government stated in December 2025 that 30 million citizens had been registered and that the identity had been carried into Digital Ethiopia 2030 with integration planned down to the lowest administrative levels ([statement](2025-12-22-fayda-digital-id-implemented-digital-2025-strategy)).

The statute itself was not amended in the window; what moved is the weight placed on it ([Digital Identification Proclamation 1284/2023](2023-04-18-ethiopia-digital-identification-proclamation-1284-2023-full-text)).

The base holds no statutory limit on state access to identity data and no redress route for a registrant, which is carried separately as a not-held position.

summary: A home-grown national civil registration architecture was set out with a phased rollout plan, and the register was extended to refugees ([presentation](2026-07-01-ethiopia-national-ecrvs-system-implementation-apai-crvs)).
developments:
Ethiopia's national electronic civil registration and vital statistics architecture — home-grown, decentralised and multi-tenant — was presented in July 2026 with its phased pilot-to-national rollout plan ([presentation](2026-07-01-ethiopia-national-ecrvs-system-implementation-apai-crvs)).

The refugee service and the Immigration and Citizenship Service ran a joint training of trainers, financed by UNICEF, implementing the updated civil registration system for refugees under the amended proclamation ([training](2026-05-09-rrs-ics-training-of-trainers-civil-family-registration-refugees)).

The city-level pilot established connectivity from the central level down to woreda level, with family and vital-event registration running digitally ([statement](2025-12-22-digital-ethiopia-2025-civil-registration-citizenship-services)).

The base holds architecture and plans, and no registration coverage rate for births or deaths.

summary: First-time central bank account numbers are now issued to new traders through the customs single window, removing a separate registration step ([service](2026-07-17-nbe-streamlines-account-number-customs-single-window)).
developments:
The central bank and the customs commission introduced a digital service issuing first-time account numbers to newly licensed importers and exporters directly through the customs electronic single window, removing a separate registration step and tightening interoperability of trade registration data ([service](2026-07-17-nbe-streamlines-account-number-customs-single-window)).

The founding instrument is the 2016 Commercial Registration and Business Licensing Proclamation, which establishes the nationwide central commercial register and trade name register and is carried as in force in the justice ministry's law catalogue ([proclamation](2016-08-05-commercial-registration-business-licensing-proclamation-980-2016)).

The base holds no count of registered businesses and no measure of how much of the register is digital.

summary: A [cloud-hosted land services platform](2025-01-01-land-et-digital-land-platform) integrated with the national identity and payment systems is in service, with nothing published about its reach.
developments:
The platform carries document upload, electronic signature and online payment, is integrated with the national identity and payment systems, and offers a mobile interface for citizens and officials ([platform](2025-01-01-land-et-digital-land-platform)).

Its own site is the held record, retrieved from a web archive after the domain failed to resolve. No parcel count, city coverage or operator is established, and a land platform whose domain does not resolve is itself the finding.

progress: Mixed, the city land system was upgraded while national rural registration was assessed as slow
summary: Addis Ababa upgraded its land system into an integrated platform ([report](2025-12-08-addis-ababa-land-bureau-reform-ilims-e-map)) while national rural registration progress was rated slow ([supervision](2025-12-10-worldbank-isr-p181591-nrlais-status)).
developments:
Addis Ababa's land bureau upgraded its online tenure and electronic map system into an Integrated Land Information Management System, reporting more than 35,000 electronic map services issued since 2016 in the Ethiopian calendar, 13 modules upgraded in the fiscal year's first quarter and over 3,100 map, mortgage-block and name-transfer services delivered ([report](2025-12-08-addis-ababa-land-bureau-reform-ilims-e-map)).

A World Bank supervision report archived in December 2025 rated reform progress on the national rural land administration information system as slow ([supervision](2025-12-10-worldbank-isr-p181591-nrlais-status)).

The system itself is the agriculture ministry's central repository for land transactions, land use and ownership ([e-services](2024-05-30-moa-e-services-nrlais)), built out through the land administration programme that ran to 2024 ([programme report](2024-01-01-reila-advancing-sustainable-land-management-ethiopia)).

The registration-coverage figures behind the slow rating are not in the captured text, so the base carries the rating without the numbers.

summary: Nationwide expansion of the digital address system to all urban centres was named a priority ([report](2026-01-01-digital-ethiopia-2030-anchors-nationwide-digital-addressing)).
developments:
The Space Science and Geospatial Institute stated that Digital Ethiopia 2030 makes nationwide expansion of the national digital address system to all urban centres a named priority ([report](2026-01-01-digital-ethiopia-2030-anchors-nationwide-digital-addressing)).

The institute's mandate to build and administer geospatial data including a digital addressing system rests on the 2022 regulation establishing it ([regulation](2022-05-09-ssgi-organization-power-duties-regulation-511-2022)).

The base holds a priority and a mandate, and no count of addresses assigned or urban centres covered.

summary: The electoral roll and its registration framework rest on the 2019 electoral proclamation, unchanged in the window ([proclamation](2019-10-16-ethiopian-electoral-proclamation-1162-2019)).
developments:
The controlling instrument is the 2019 electoral proclamation, which defines the electoral roll and the voter and candidate registration framework and confirms the national election board as the impartial election administration ([proclamation](2019-10-16-ethiopian-electoral-proclamation-1162-2019)).

The voter and candidate registration system and the count of voters registered for the seventh general election are carried on the ledger from April 2026 and nothing in the window moved them.

The base holds no statement on whether the electoral roll is checked against the civil register or the national digital identity.

summary: 444 of 492 woredas use the safety-net management system, and a funded successor project committed to stronger digital tools ([restructuring paper](2025-10-20-ethiopia-seasn-restructuring-paper)).
developments:
The October 2025 restructuring paper for the adaptive safety net project records 444 of 492 woredas using the management information system for programme tracking, 5.1 of 7.9 million beneficiaries' data synchronised to the federal system, and 252 woredas on electronic payments, with full operationalisation targeted for the end of December 2025 ([restructuring paper](2025-10-20-ethiopia-seasn-restructuring-paper)).

The World Bank board approved the US$200m sixth Productive Safety Net Project in March 2026, committing to stronger digital tools and improved monitoring behind delivery ([approval](2026-03-03-ethiopia-psnp6-new-phase-safety-nets)).

The base holds no statement that the December 2025 target was met, so the most recent coverage figures are from before the deadline they were measured against.

summary: A smart court system runs across 24 federal branches, and a criminal record information system gained a steering committee ([launch statement](2025-10-10-ethiopia-digital-2030-smart-court-system)).
developments:
The Federal Supreme Court has developed a Smart Court System with automated voice-to-text transcription, virtual hearings, a network operations centre and an integrated case management system letting litigants track cases digitally, operating across 24 federal branches with regional expansion planned ([launch statement](2025-10-10-ethiopia-digital-2030-smart-court-system)).

The justice ministry announced that a project steering committee set strategic directions for the Criminal Record Information Management System in April 2026, with no coverage figures disclosed ([announcement](2026-04-20-ethiopia-crims-project-steering-committee)).

The standing programmatic instrument is the National Justice Sector Transformation Roadmap, whose ten pillars include digital justice transformation ([roadmap](2025-04-04-ethiopia-justice-sector-transformation-roadmap)).

The base holds branch counts, not case volumes, and nothing on whether regional courts have followed.

summary: A startup proclamation created statutory designation, a grant programme and a credit-guarantee fund ([proclamation](2025-09-02-ethiopia-startup-proclamation-1396-2025)).
developments:
The Startup Proclamation 1396/2025, published in the federal gazette in September 2025, creates a designation for startups and for "ecosystem builders", a digital startup portal, a national startup designation committee, a startup grant programme, a credit-guarantee fund and a fund of funds ([proclamation](2025-09-02-ethiopia-startup-proclamation-1396-2025)).

The Addis Ababa e-mobility startup Dodai closed a US$13m Series A in April 2026, US$8m of equity and US$5m of debt ([announcement](2026-04-28-dodai-13-million-series-a)).

The Artificial Intelligence University Innovation Pod was inaugurated in February 2026 with the AI institute, UNDP and Addis Ababa University, adding domestic research and incubation infrastructure ([launch](2026-02-16-ethiopia-launches-ai-unipod)).

The base holds no count of designated startups or of grants made under the new statute.

summary: International card acceptance [went live through the national switch](2025-11-30-ethswitch-15-year-digital-payment-vision) in November 2025, and the payments strategy [proposes first outbound transfers](2025-12-09 Ethiopia launches National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030).
developments:
The national switch and an international card network brought international acceptance live in November 2025 ([card acceptance](2025-11-30-ethswitch-15-year-digital-payment-vision)).

The payments strategy published a fortnight later proposes the country's first outbound cross-border transfers, which are not currently permitted ([payments strategy](2025-12-09 Ethiopia launches National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030)).

No transaction volume, corridor or remittance figure is held, and the base records nothing on inbound remittance channels, which are the larger cross-border flow.

summary: An [instant payment system](2026-02-13-ethiopia-launches-national-instant-payments) launched in February 2026 across 32 banks and 12 microfinance institutions, with merchant and cash-out services added since.
developments:
The national instant payment system carries account-to-account and wallet-to-wallet transfers with a national quick-response standard and aliases ([instant payments](2026-02-13-ethiopia-launches-national-instant-payments)).

The switch behind it links the challenger wallet to more than 30 banks and wallets in real time, with merchant payments at more than 50,000 merchants ([switch integration](2026-03-30 M-PESA Ethiopia surges 258% as EthSwitch fuels growth)).

Cardless cash withdrawals with one bank went live in August 2026, authorised in the app before cash is dispensed ([cardless withdrawals](2026-08-11-mpesa-ethiopia-cardless-atm-withdrawals)), and prepaid electricity became purchasable in the wallet in July ([electricity payments](2026-07-29-m-pesa-ethiopia-launches-prepaid-electricity-payments-through-super-app)).

summary: A national digital financial literacy campaign reached 525 civil servants drawn from 26 public institutions ([campaign](2026-04-07-uncdf-closing-digital-finance-gap-women-civil-servant)).
developments:
The Ministry of Innovation and Technology, with UNCDF, ran a nationwide digital financial literacy campaign reaching 525 participants from 26 public institutions, targeted at women civil servants ([campaign](2026-04-07-uncdf-closing-digital-finance-gap-women-civil-servant)).

The government set a target of 80% of government employees digitally skilled by 2030 under Digital Ethiopia 2030 ([target](2025-12-22-gcs-startups-digital-skills-development)).

The earlier position was a mandate to develop civil-servant courses under the Digital Foundations project, whose digital-literacy and training-of-trainers activities were marked complete ([aide-memoire](2025-02-01-ethiopia-digital-foundations-project-aide-memoire)).

The base holds no measurement of how many civil servants have been trained against the 2030 target.

summary: The national coding initiative passed 5,005,146 enrolments, ahead of its target date ([milestone](2026-06-11-pm-abiy-5-million-ethiopian-coders-milestone)).
developments:
The 5 Million Ethiopian Coders Initiative passed its enrolment target ahead of schedule at 5,005,146 enrolments in programming, data analysis, Android development and AI fundamentals, and a 7-million target was set ([milestone](2026-06-11-pm-abiy-5-million-ethiopian-coders-milestone)).

Digital Ethiopia 2030 was launched in December 2025 with quantified population digital-literacy and internet-penetration targets, superseding Digital Ethiopia 2025 ([launch](2025-12-20-pm-abiy-launches-digital-ethiopia-2030)); the government states these as 70% population digital literacy and 10 million citizens trained by 2030 ([targets](2025-12-22-gcs-startups-digital-skills-development)).

The standing measured baseline is the 2022 national digital literacy maturity survey, on which 60.27% of those surveyed could use a computer, tablet or smartphone and 53.71% used the internet ([survey, as cited in the education strategy](2023-09-01-ethiopia-digital-education-strategy-2023-2028)).

The base holds no repeat of that survey, so training enrolments are the only movement actually measured.

summary: A EUR21m programme to digitalise technical and vocational training launched, and a national digital-skills needs assessment was validated ([DESTA](2025-11-28-giz-desta-launch-digitalised-tvet)).
developments:
The DESTA initiative launched in November 2025 — EUR21m from Germany, the EU and Finland with the Ministry of Labor and Skills — modernising digital learning infrastructure and trainer digital competencies across TVET institutions in five regions ([launch](2025-11-28-giz-desta-launch-digitalised-tvet)).

UNESCO, the Ministry of Labor and Skills and the Federal TVET Institute validated a digital-skills training-needs assessment for TVET teachers and students in July 2026, identifying competency gaps and an action plan ([workshop](2026-08-07-unesco-strengthening-digital-skills-ethiopia-tvet)).

The standing framework is the Digital Education Strategy 2023-2028, which sets digital-literacy objectives for teachers and students across general and secondary education ([strategy](2023-09-01-ethiopia-digital-education-strategy-2023-2028)).

The base holds no count of TVET institutions reached or trainers certified under either.

summary: The national coding initiative passed five million enrolments and a first artificial-intelligence startup cohort graduated ([milestone](2026-06-11-pm-abiy-5-million-ethiopian-coders-milestone)).
developments:
The 5 Million Ethiopian Coders Initiative, launched in July 2024, passed its target ahead of schedule at 5,005,146 enrolments, with a 7-million target set for August 2026 ([milestone](2026-06-11-pm-abiy-5-million-ethiopian-coders-milestone)).

The Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute graduated the first cohort of a six-month AI startup programme, which exhibited solutions in healthcare, education, transport, language technology, smart cities, finance and human development ([graduation](2026-07-25-ethiopia-ai-skilled-workforce-deputy-pm)).

The Digital Foundations project's capacity-building component was rated satisfactory, with its own supervision recording that the impact needs to be systematically documented ([aide-memoire](2025-02-01-ethiopia-digital-foundations-project-aide-memoire)).

The base holds enrolments and graduations, not placements: nothing measures how many of these graduates enter the digital economy.

summary: The statistics service formalised public data access as a standing dissemination function ([mandate](2026-05-06-ess-statistical-data-dissemination-and-access)).
developments:
The Ethiopian Statistics Service now carries statistical data dissemination and access as a dedicated departmental function, covering its data bank, microdata repositories, web portals, anonymisation, public use files and dashboards ([mandate](2026-05-06-ess-statistical-data-dissemination-and-access)).

Ethiopia OpenAgriNet launched in February 2026 as an open-standards, consent-based agricultural data platform ([launch](2026-02-03-ethiopia-openagrinet-launch)).

The last authoritative statement on the general-purpose portal is from 2018: data.gov.et launched in March 2016 with 29 datasets posted in open format, three of five planned citizen-facing applications delivered, and the open-data policy guideline still in draft ([supervision report](2018-07-08-world-bank-isr-ethiopia-open-data-initiative)).

The base holds no later status for data.gov.et and no dataset count for it after 2018, so what moved here are the sectoral platforms rather than the national portal.

summary: Ethiopian technical staff were trained on satellite crop and water monitoring platforms, and a supplier agreement for Earth-observation data was signed ([workshop](2026-07-06-cropwatch-etwatch-training-workshop-ethiopia)).
developments:
A four-day workshop in Addis Ababa in June 2026 trained more than 50 technical staff from seven African countries, Ethiopia among them, on the CropWatch and ETWatch satellite crop and water monitoring platforms, covering crop condition, evapotranspiration and yield prediction; it was co-hosted by the Agricultural Transformation Institute and the Ethiopian Institute of Agricultural Research ([workshop](2026-07-06-cropwatch-etwatch-training-workshop-ethiopia)).

Japan's Axelspace signed a memorandum with the Ethiopian firm Jethi Software Development in January 2026 to supply Earth-observation data and build a local utilisation framework — a private agreement, not government to government ([memorandum](2026-01-15-axelspace-jethi-mou-satellite-data-ethiopia)).

The standing government tool is LEAP, which converts satellite and ground agro-meteorological data into crop and rangeland production estimates and safety-net contingent-financing triggers ([LEAP](2026-08-28-edrmc-leap-satellite-early-warning)).

The base holds no dated statement of LEAP's current operating status; the page describing it is undated.

summary: An AI-driven multi-hazard early-warning system combining Chinese satellite products with local station data is being operationalised ([interview](2026-07-25-xinhua-mazu-china-ai-ethiopia-meteorological)).
developments:
The meteorology institute's deputy director general describes the MAZU system, from the China Meteorological Administration, as installed, configured and being operationalised, combining FengYun satellite products with local station data for downscaled nowcasting, and as the first such deployment in Africa ([interview](2026-07-25-xinhua-mazu-china-ai-ethiopia-meteorological)).

Addis Ababa is one of five pilot cities for the Urban Flash Flood Forecasting System, which combines satellite observations with nowcasting and was advanced at a regional workshop in March 2026 ([workshop](2026-04-02-wmo-urban-flash-flood-forecasting-eastern-africa)).

The standing operational position is the institute's own satellite product set — natural-colour and dust imagery, precipitation rate, infrared imagery and rapidly developing thunderstorm nowcasting ([products](2026-08-28-emi-satellite-imagery)).

The account of MAZU is the operator's own, carried by state media, with nothing on the base testing forecast performance.
