progress: Mixed, the demographic and health survey reported in full while the population census remains that of 2007
summary: The fifth demographic and health survey reported ([summary report](2026-07-08-edhs-2024-25-summary-report)); the census behind current population figures is still 2007's ([census](2024-10-16-ess-population-census)).
developments:
The 2024/25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey released its key indicators in January 2026 ([key indicators](2026-01-01-edhs-2024-25-key-indicators-report)) and its full summary report in July 2026, covering 22,540 households surveyed between August 2024 and April 2025 ([summary report](2026-07-08-edhs-2024-25-summary-report)).

The statistics service records three national censuses — 1984, 1994 and 2007 — and states that current population estimates are still projections from the 2007 census ([census page](2024-10-16-ess-population-census)).

The base holds no date for a fourth census and no statement from the statistics service on when one will be held, so the survey programme is delivering against a population denominator that is now nearly two decades old.

progress: No change, the strategy on the base expired in 2019/20 and no successor is held
summary: The strategy of record is the second national statistics-development strategy, whose period ran to 2019/20 ([NSDS II](2016-07-01-ethiopia-nsds-ii-2015-16-2019-20)).
developments:
The second National Strategy for the Development of Statistics, covering 2015/16 to 2019/20, was adopted by the Statistics Council and succeeded the 2009 first strategy ([NSDS II](2016-07-01-ethiopia-nsds-ii-2015-16-2019-20)).

What moved in the window was legislative rather than strategic: the House of People's Representatives approved the Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation on 30 June 2026, intended to strengthen the service's independence and align the national statistical system with international principles ([approval](2026-06-30-ethiopian-statistical-service-proclamation-approved)).

No third strategy was located at the probe date of 28 August 2026, so the planning instrument has been out of period for six years while the statutory basis is being replaced.

summary: The statistics service took the lead of a regional migration data working group under a signed data-sharing protocol ([workshop](2025-08-28-igad-workshop-migration-data-sharing-mou-ethiopia)).
developments:
A three-day IGAD workshop operationalised the memorandum and Migration and Displacement Data Sharing Protocol signed by Ethiopian institutions in January 2025, with the statistics service empowered to lead the Migration Data Technical Working Group ([workshop](2025-08-28-igad-workshop-migration-data-sharing-mou-ethiopia)).

The standing framework is the Code of Practice for Official Statistics, which expressly recognises administrative records, registers and government systems as sources of official statistics, assigning the statistics service the operational role and the planning ministry the regulatory one ([code of practice](2023-10-01-code-of-practice-official-statistics-ethiopia)).

The base holds the mandate and one sectoral working group, and no count of which administrative systems actually feed published statistics.

summary: A successor statistics proclamation was approved by the House on 30 June 2026, replacing the 2005 statute ([approval](2026-06-30-ethiopian-statistical-service-proclamation-approved)).
developments:
The Council of Ministers referred the draft Ethiopian Statistics Proclamation to the House of People's Representatives on 26 May 2026 ([referral](2026-05-26-council-of-ministers-refers-statistics-proclamation)), and the House approved it on 30 June 2026, intended to strengthen the statistics service's independence and align the national statistical system with international statistical principles ([approval](2026-06-30-ethiopian-statistical-service-proclamation-approved)).

The statute it replaces is Proclamation 442/2005, which established the Central Statistics Authority as an autonomous federal agency with legal personality and defined the national statistical programme ([Proclamation 442/2005](2005-04-20-central-statistics-authority-establishment-proclamation-442-2005)).

No gazette text or proclamation number for the new law had been located at the probe date of 28 August 2026, so what is held is the approval, not the enacted text.

summary: Addis Ababa launched an integrated civil registration and residency system reaching down to woreda level ([launch](2025-12-05-addis-ababa-launches-integrated-digital-civil-service-system)).
developments:
The Addis Ababa city administration launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology, developed by the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, integrating vital-events registration with residency identification, with implementation scheduled across 50 woredas from 8 December 2025 ([launch](2025-12-05-addis-ababa-launches-integrated-digital-civil-service-system)).

The government's own account describes the pilot as having established connectivity from the central level down to woreda level using locally developed applications, with family and vital-event registration, resident services and verification running digitally ([statement](2025-12-22-digital-ethiopia-2025-civil-registration-citizenship-services)).

The base holds this for the capital only. Nothing states how many of the country's woredas outside Addis Ababa keep records digitally, and the city's own one-stop service centres are carried on the city administration's account rather than a national programme.

summary: A matched study found measurably better maternal and child health delivery in woredas running the digitised community health information system ([study](2026-05-28-plos-one-echis-maternal-child-health-impact-study)).
developments:
A propensity-score-matching study published in May 2026, on household data collected in July and August 2024, found woredas implementing the electronic community health information system had higher modern contraceptive use by 13.0 percentage points, institutional deliveries by 8.9 points and full vaccination coverage by 14.6 points than non-implementing woredas ([study](2026-05-28-plos-one-echis-maternal-child-health-impact-study)).

The national health information system reached 72% of districts, with more than 2,975 institute, regional and woreda staff trained, alongside a new emergency-management system and event-based surveillance ([report](2025-10-31-who-afro-ethiopia-digitalizes-health-emergency-information-systems)).

The health ministry's annual sector performance report for 2024/25 carries a dedicated digital health chapter ([annual report](2025-10-01-moh-annual-health-sector-performance-report-2017-efy)).

The base holds district coverage, not health-post coverage, so how far digitisation reaches the last mile is not stated.

progress: Advanced, on national police identity workflows rather than measured rural station coverage
summary: The police referral application and unmanned service centres were connected to the national digital identity ([statement](2026-03-12-fayda-enhances-police-operations-crime-prevention)).
developments:
The Federal Police Commission, meeting with deputy commissioners from all regional states, stated that the police referral application and unmanned police service centres are connected to the Fayda national digital identity, converting manual identification and investigation tasks into digital workflows ([statement](2026-03-12-fayda-enhances-police-operations-crime-prevention)).

The Prime Minister announced the first unmanned or smart police service in February 2026 as part of the Digital Ethiopia 2030 law-enforcement reform ([message](2026-02-09-pm-abiy-message-smart-police-service-launch)); that is a pilot in the capital.

The base holds no count of rural police stations with digital case or record systems, and nothing distinguishes rural from urban in either account, so this indicator rests on a national identity link and an urban pilot.

summary: An open-source education information system was adopted, with initial implementation covering schools and woredas in four regions ([launch](2025-11-13-ethiopia-launches-dhis2-for-education)).
developments:
Ethiopia adopted DHIS2 for Education, an open-source education management information system, with initial implementation covering schools, woredas and zones in four regions and the explicit aim of operationalising the ministry's national system at local levels ([launch](2025-11-13-ethiopia-launches-dhis2-for-education)).

A US$69m additional financing package approved in March 2026 integrates all 57 refugee primary schools into the national education system, including into the national education information system, with US$750,000 earmarked for enhancement and disaggregated reporting ([programme paper](2026-03-18-ethiopia-etol-additional-financing-program-paper)).

The funded reform behind the rollout is the girls' education and learning programme, which names digitisation of the education information system as a reform strand with rollout to primary schools planned across 4,500 schools in 150 woredas ([programme document](2024-02-16-step-programme-document-girls-education-2024-2028)).

The base holds plans and initial regions, and no count of primary schools actually reporting through the system.

progress: No change, a first statement of the position with no earlier figure behind it
summary: Rural land registration runs on second-level certification and a national rural land administration information system ([programme report](2024-01-01-reila-advancing-sustainable-land-management-ethiopia)).
developments:
The land administration programme's completion report, covering 2011 to 2024, records the digitalisation of rural land administration through second-level land certification and the National Rural Land Administration Information System, endorsed as the national land registry system ([programme report](2024-01-01-reila-advancing-sustainable-land-management-ethiopia)).

The captured text of that report reaches only its table of contents, so the number of woredas operating the system is not something the base can state, and its publication date is a proxy taken from the stated project period.

The base holds no separate account of registry offices outside land — civil, business or vehicle registration at woreda level — so this indicator rests on one sector.

summary: Refugee schools are being integrated into the national education information system under a funded package ([programme paper](2026-03-18-ethiopia-etol-additional-financing-program-paper)).
developments:
A US$69m additional financing package approved in March 2026 integrates all 57 refugee primary schools into the national education system, including full integration of refugee learners into the national education information system, with US$750,000 earmarked for enhancement and disaggregated reporting ([programme paper](2026-03-18-ethiopia-etol-additional-financing-program-paper)).

The adoption of DHIS2 for Education in November 2025 was framed explicitly as operationalising the ministry's national education information system at local levels so that local data can be used where it is collected ([launch](2025-11-13-ethiopia-launches-dhis2-for-education)).

Both are integrations into one sector's system. The base holds nothing on education data exchanging with the national data exchange platform, the civil register or the digital identity.

summary: A US$200m successor safety-net project moved the national social registry from appraisal into funded implementation ([approval](2026-03-03-ethiopia-psnp6-new-phase-safety-nets)).
developments:
The World Bank board approved the sixth Productive Safety Net Project in March 2026, a US$200m credit committing to stronger digital tools and improved monitoring behind safety-net delivery and moving the national social registry from appraisal into funded implementation ([approval](2026-03-03-ethiopia-psnp6-new-phase-safety-nets)).

The founding requirement is the 2023 digital identity financing agreement, which requires a digital stack including a whole-of-government data exchange platform and open APIs, and prioritises integration into public services including social protection ([financing agreement](2023-12-20-ethiopia-digital-id-financing-agreement)).

The base holds the commitment and the money. It holds no statement that the social registry actually exchanges data with the identity system, the civil register or the payment rails.

progress: No change, a first statement of the position with nothing measuring registration at birth
summary: Birth registration is being extended operationally, including backlog clearance for refugee children in Afar ([mission](2026-04-26-rrs-afar-birth-registration-mission)).
developments:
A joint field mission by the refugee service with UNICEF, UNHCR and the Immigration and Citizenship Service cleared birth-registration backlogs and assessed service delivery for refugee children in Semera and Asayita refugee camp in April 2026 ([mission](2026-04-26-rrs-afar-birth-registration-mission)).

The government's own account of civil registration digitalisation describes family and vital-event registration running digitally from the central level down to woreda level ([statement](2025-12-22-digital-ethiopia-2025-civil-registration-citizenship-services)).

The base holds no birth-registration rate, and nothing states whether a registered birth produces a national identity number, so the link this indicator asks about is not evidenced either way.

summary: The customs commission describes its services as fully digitalised, on an electronic single window integrating more than 70 institutions ([interview](2026-02-25-ethiopian-customs-commission-fully-digitalized)).
developments:
The customs commission's deputy commissioner states that services are fully digitalised, with an electronic single window integrating more than 70 institutions and letting traders submit import and export requirements together, and a smart border customs management system with AI-enabled cameras covering about 50 kilometres at border stations ([interview](2026-02-25-ethiopian-customs-commission-fully-digitalized)).

A central bank directive of May 2026 requires the customs commission to use or integrate with the foreign exchange monitoring system to record and trace franco valuta imports digitally ([directive](2026-05-29-import-franco-valuta-directive-fvd-01-2026)).

The transport ministry supplied electronic seals to enhance the commission's electronic cargo tracking system for origin-to-destination monitoring ([donation](2025-12-20-ethiopia-electronic-cargo-tracking-system-equipment)).

The claim of full digitalisation is the commission's own, with no independent measurement of clearance times or coverage on the base.

summary: The education information system gained an adopted open-source platform and funded enhancement ([launch](2025-11-13-ethiopia-launches-dhis2-for-education)).
developments:
Ethiopia adopted DHIS2 for Education in November 2025, with initial implementation covering schools, woredas and zones in four regions, aimed at operationalising the ministry's national system at local levels ([launch](2025-11-13-ethiopia-launches-dhis2-for-education)).

A March 2026 additional financing package earmarked US$750,000 for enhancement of the education information system and disaggregated reporting, alongside integration of all 57 refugee primary schools ([programme paper](2026-03-18-ethiopia-etol-additional-financing-program-paper)).

The evidence that the system exists and is operationally maintained is the ministry's own annual statistical abstract, produced by its education information and technology office and describing the system as available at decentralised levels ([abstract](2023-10-01-ethiopia-education-statistics-annual-abstract-2022-23)).

No statute establishing the system was located; the ministry's mandate rests on its own establishing proclamation.

summary: Federal public bodies must now accept payment from any licensed provider ([directive](2025-05-26-directive-1069-2025-mandatory-payment-acceptance)), and an electronic invoicing layer was established.
developments:
Directive 1069/2025, signed by the finance minister in May 2025, requires all federal public bodies to accept payment from any licensed payment service provider — cards, prepaid instruments, mobile wallets, mobile and internet banking and bank transfers — and to integrate their collection systems with authorised gateways ([directive](2025-05-26-directive-1069-2025-mandatory-payment-acceptance)).

Directive 1142/2026 established the electronic invoicing administration layer, requiring taxpayers to use an authorised electronic invoice registration system and setting rules for sales-registration system providers ([directive](2026-06-09-electronic-invoicing-system-administration-directive-1142-2026)).

The national payments conference of December 2025 recorded the launch of the draft national digital payments strategy and of the instant payment system, the rails both directives depend on ([conference](2025-12-09-ethiopia-digital-payment-conference-2-launch-ndps-2)).

The base holds the obligations, not compliance: nothing counts the public bodies that have integrated.

summary: The central bank moved from rule to enforcement, ordering banks and payment issuers to implement fraud-warning measures ([campaign](2026-03-25-nbe-customer-fraud-awareness-campaign)).
developments:
The central bank launched a customer fraud awareness messaging campaign in March 2026, instructing banks, payment instrument issuers and microfinance institutions to implement fraud-warning measures under the financial consumer protection directive's own articles, in response to a rise in impersonation scams over messaging apps, text and telephone ([campaign](2026-03-25-nbe-customer-fraud-awareness-campaign)).

It ran its first annual financial literacy week in October 2025 under a consumer-protection theme, with outreach on mobile money use and digital risks such as fraud and data misuse ([launch](2025-10-27-nbe-financial-literacy-week-2025)).

The operative instrument is the financial consumer protection directive issued in August 2020, which covers mobile wallets and mobile and internet banking explicitly and sets liability for unauthorised and mistaken transactions ([directive](2020-08-25-financial-consumer-protection-directive-292-2021)).

The base holds no complaint volumes, redress outcomes or fraud losses, so enforcement is visible and its effect is not.

summary: Finance, the central bank and the national switch convened government institutions to operationalise interoperable government payments ([report](2026-07-17-ethiopia-nationwide-rollout-interoperable-government-payments)).
developments:
In July 2026 the finance ministry, the central bank and the national switch convened technical teams from government institutions to operationalise a unified implementation framework for interoperable person-to-government and government-to-person payments, aligned to the national digital payments strategy ([report](2026-07-17-ethiopia-nationwide-rollout-interoperable-government-payments)).

The rails behind it were launched at the December 2025 payments conference, which recorded both the draft national digital payments strategy and the instant payment system ([conference](2025-12-09-ethiopia-digital-payment-conference-2-launch-ndps-2)).

The national switch's own annual report for the year to June 2025 sets out its mandate over interoperability, the national payment scheme and the national payment gateway, and carries government payment work as a project under implementation rather than a live service ([annual report](2025-10-01-ethswitch-annual-report-2024-25)).

The base holds no volume or value of government payments actually made over these rails.

summary: The national social registry moved from a concept-stage activity into funded implementation ([approval](2026-03-03-ethiopia-psnp6-new-phase-safety-nets)).
developments:
The concept-stage project document of June 2025 named development and rollout of a national social registry as a project activity, showing it as a build rather than an established system at appraisal ([project document](2025-06-20-worldbank-psnp6-project-information-document)).

The World Bank board approved the US$200m sixth Productive Safety Net Project in March 2026, moving that registry into funded implementation ([approval](2026-03-03-ethiopia-psnp6-new-phase-safety-nets)).

The programme's existing management information system is further advanced: 444 of 492 woredas use it for programme tracking and 5.1 of 7.9 million beneficiaries' data had been synchronised to the federal system, with 252 woredas on electronic payments ([restructuring paper](2025-10-20-ethiopia-seasn-restructuring-paper)).

A registry and a programme management system are different things, and the base holds no enrolment figure for the registry itself.

summary: A directive materially widened who must enter the value-added tax register, with a 30-day window for those already affected ([directive](2025-09-02-vat-registration-directive-1104-2025)).
developments:
Directive 1104/2025, issued by the finance ministry in September 2025 under the value-added tax proclamation, expanded who must register: Category A taxpayers, mandatory and voluntary book-keepers, businesses with turnover above two million birr, and specified professional-service providers below that threshold, with a 30-day registration window for existing affected taxpayers ([directive](2025-09-02-vat-registration-directive-1104-2025)).

The statutory basis is the 2016 federal tax administration proclamation, which requires taxpayer registration and establishes the taxpayer identification number ([proclamation](2016-08-20-federal-tax-administration-proclamation-983-2016)).

The base holds no count of registered taxpayers before or after the widening, so the size of the change is not measurable from it.

summary: The 2025 creditor-committee memorandum moved into implementation, with a bilateral agreement and a bondholder agreement in principle ([agreement](2026-06-29-ethiopia-agreement-in-principle-bondholders-2024-notes)).
developments:
Ethiopia concluded a memorandum of understanding with its Official Creditor Committee under the G20 Common Framework on 2 July 2025, formalising a debt treatment worth over US$3.5bn to be implemented through bilateral agreements ([memorandum](2025-07-02-ethiopia-mou-official-creditor-committee-g20-common-framework)).

The first of those bilateral agreements was signed with Italy in Rome on 18 March 2026 ([agreement](2026-03-18-ethiopia-italy-debt-restructuring-agreement)).

On 29 June 2026 Ethiopia reached agreement in principle with the ad hoc committee of holders of its US$1bn 2024 notes on restructuring terms ([agreement](2026-06-29-ethiopia-agreement-in-principle-bondholders-2024-notes)).

These are financial rather than digital instruments. The base holds no memorandum tying this financing to the digital programme, so the relevance here is fiscal room rather than a digital commitment.

summary: The EU announced resumed budget support and a EUR150m digital economy package at the April 2026 business forum ([announcement](2026-04-20-eu-sikela-business-forum-ethiopia-package)).
developments:
At the EU-Ethiopia Business Forum of 20-22 April 2026 the EU announced the resumption of over EUR140m in budget support, a EUR150m digital economy package and EUR130m in new lending from the European Investment Bank, and noted results delivered under the EUR269m renewable energy and digitalisation programme ([announcement](2026-04-20-eu-sikela-business-forum-ethiopia-package)).

That programme was signed in September 2025 on the margins of the Africa Climate Summit, a EUR120m contribution from the EU and the French development agency to modernise power and digital infrastructure ([signing](2025-09-08-eu-france-ethiopia-rised-120m-agreement)).

The governing framework is the EU's multiannual indicative programme for 2024-2027, adopted in September 2023 ([programme](2023-09-29-eu-mip-ethiopia-2024-2027)).

The digital economy package is an announced commitment; the base holds no signed instrument or disbursement against it.

progress: Advanced, on diplomatic and research cooperation rather than on any digital instrument
summary: A memorandum was signed between the two states' diplomatic academies, and technology appears as a dialogue theme rather than a commitment ([dialogue](2026-06-28-wam-hili-africa-dialogue-uae-ethiopia-mou)).
developments:
The second Hili Africa Dialogue concluded in Addis Ababa in June 2026, at which a memorandum of understanding was signed between the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy and Ethiopia's Institute of Foreign Affairs for research and capacity-building cooperation; its sessions discussed expanding cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence ([dialogue](2026-06-28-wam-hili-africa-dialogue-uae-ethiopia-mou)).

The standing bilateral position is the joint ministerial statement of 6 January 2026, which reaffirms a comprehensive strategic partnership and covers Sudan, the climate presidency and water, and names nothing digital ([statement](2026-01-06-uae-ethiopia-joint-ministerial-statement)).

A December 2025 ambassadorial meeting explored cooperation in trade, investment, renewable energy and technology, agreeing to maintain momentum through the Joint Ministerial Commission ([meeting](2025-12-26-ena-ethiopia-uae-strategic-partnership-meeting)).

The engagement is real and the digital instrument is not: no Gulf memorandum, investment or ministerial readout names Ethiopian digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence or payments.

progress: Advanced, on a security-clearance directive rather than on any statute addressed to artificial intelligence
summary: An implementing directive gave the security agency power to designate new and emerging technology products for clearance ([directive](2026-05-01-insa-it-products-security-clearance-directive-1135-2026)).
developments:
Directive 1135/2026, made under the Information Technology Products Security Clearance and Control Proclamation, creates security clearance, permit and monitoring procedures for restricted and prohibited information technology products and provides for the designation of new or emerging products — a power wide enough to reach advanced artificial-intelligence systems ([directive](2026-05-01-insa-it-products-security-clearance-directive-1135-2026)).

The only instrument addressed to artificial intelligence as such remains the National Artificial Intelligence Policy adopted by the Council of Ministers in June 2024, a policy rather than a binding statute ([policy](2024-06-01-ethiopia-national-artificial-intelligence-policy)).

The base holds no AI act, no draft bill and no regulator with an artificial-intelligence mandate, so what governs AI here is import control and general policy.

progress: No change, the recommended broadband plan is still not held and what moved sits alongside it
summary: A government-commissioned assessment recommended a broadband plan be developed; none has been established since ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)).
developments:
The 2023 e-government assessment commissioned by the innovation and technology ministry recommended that a broadband plan be developed to guide infrastructure deployment ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)). No such plan was located at the probe date of 28 August 2026.

What moved sits alongside it. The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 in November 2025, which commits to nationwide high-speed broadband as part of the successor national digital strategy ([approval](2025-11-29-council-of-ministers-approves-digital-ethiopia-2030-strategy)).

Ethiopia's broadband mapping system was introduced at a national event in October 2025, bringing the Economic Commission for Africa, the EU delegation and the ITU together to build the infrastructure evidence base for future broadband policy ([event](2025-10-14-africa-bb-maps-national-event-ethiopia)).

A commitment inside a general strategy and a mapping tool are not a broadband strategy, and the base does not treat them as one.

summary: The security agency announced a home-grown government cloud framed expressly as implementing data localisation ([announcement](2026-04-06-insa-empowering-ethiopia-digital-sovereignty-gotera-cloud)).
developments:
The Information Network Security Administration announced Gotera Cloud, a home-grown government cloud offering infrastructure, platform, software and backup services, framed expressly as implementing data localisation and data sovereignty ([announcement](2026-04-06-insa-empowering-ethiopia-digital-sovereignty-gotera-cloud)).

The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 in November 2025, a strategy centred on sovereign national cloud and domestic data governance ([approval](2025-11-29-council-of-ministers-approves-digital-ethiopia-2030-strategy)).

The base holds an infrastructure build and a strategy commitment, and no rule: nothing on the record requires any class of data to be stored in Ethiopia, and the data protection proclamation's cross-border provisions are not framed as localisation.

progress: No change, the open-data policy guideline recorded as draft in 2018 is still not held as adopted
summary: A government-commissioned assessment recommended reviving the failed common open-data portal ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)).
developments:
The 2023 e-government assessment found no open-data sharing between institutions and recommended reviving the common open-data portal ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)).

Digital Ethiopia 2030, approved by the Council of Ministers in November 2025, commits to a national data authority and structured government data ([approval](2025-11-29-council-of-ministers-approves-digital-ethiopia-2030-strategy)).

Ethiopia OpenAgriNet launched in February 2026 on open standards with consent-based data governance, the clearest sectoral operationalisation of open-data principles in the window ([launch](2026-02-03-ethiopia-openagrinet-launch)).

The open-data policy guideline was recorded as still in draft in 2018 ([supervision report](2018-07-08-world-bank-isr-ethiopia-open-data-initiative)) and the base holds no later statement that it was adopted, so the policy instrument itself has not moved in eight years.

summary: Ethiopia completed the validation stage of its continental free trade implementation review, intended to guide domestic regulatory alignment ([validation](2026-08-06-ethiopia-validates-afcfta-protocol-trade-in-goods)).
developments:
Ethiopia completed the final validation stage of its African Continental Free Trade Area implementation review in August 2026, using the continental review matrix, intended to guide policy and regulatory reform aligning domestic rules with continental trade commitments ([validation](2026-08-06-ethiopia-validates-afcfta-protocol-trade-in-goods)).

At the third IGAD ministerial conference on labour and migration in October 2025, with Ethiopia's state minister among signatories, the communique welcomed a single visa initiative through harmonised visa systems and recorded that millions of the region's citizens lack legal identification or hold identity documents unsuitable for the digital age ([communique](2025-10-22-igad-ministerial-communique-labour-employment-migration)).

Ethiopia ratified the 2023 IGAD Treaty in April 2024, the operative instrument for its standing in the regional harmonisation framework ([ratification](2024-04-19-ethiopia-ratifies-new-igad-treaty)).

These are commitments to harmonise rather than harmonised rules; the base holds no domestic instrument amended to match a regional one.

summary: The government interoperability framework remains the standing instrument, listed as approved and not superseded ([repository entry](2019-01-01-ea-2019-ethiopian-government-interoperability-framework)).
developments:
The interoperability framework of record is the Ethiopian Government Interoperability Framework, carried as approved in the innovation and technology ministry's own guidelines and standards repository ([repository entry](2019-01-01-ea-2019-ethiopian-government-interoperability-framework)).

Digital Ethiopia 2030, approved in November 2025, commits to interoperable digital systems ([approval](2025-11-29-council-of-ministers-approves-digital-ethiopia-2030-strategy)), but names no standard and supersedes no framework.

The repository entry is a document-library listing rather than the framework text, so the base holds that the framework exists and is current without holding what it requires.

summary: A secure corruption reporting and case-tracking channel launched across the state holding company's portfolio ([Adera](2026-01-01-eih-adera-corruption-reporting-system)).
developments:
Adera launched in January 2026 as a secure corruption reporting and case-tracking channel for the public and for employees across Ethiopian Investment Holdings' portfolio companies, with anonymity and report tracking ([Adera](2026-01-01-eih-adera-corruption-reporting-system)).

The unified public service application was inaugurated in June 2026, described by the Prime Minister as bringing services from across institutions onto one platform, saving citizens' time and closing corruption gaps ([inauguration](2026-06-20-pm-abiy-inaugurates-mesob-application)).

Both are channels into the state rather than published feedback: the base holds no complaint volumes, response times or resolution rates for either, so whether they function as feedback loops is not evidenced.

summary: A national dialogue conference of around 4,000 participants concluded in August 2026, deliberating eight national agenda items ([conclusion](2026-08-22-national-dialogue-conference-concludes)).
developments:
The Ethiopian National Dialogue Conference ran from 15 July to 22 August 2026 with around 4,000 participants deliberating eight national agenda items, and submitted its recommendations to the National Dialogue Commission ([conclusion](2026-08-22-national-dialogue-conference-concludes)).

The World Bank ran stakeholder consultations on its 2027-2036 country partnership framework across government, development partners, the private sector, civil society and regional governments, with an online window in May 2026 ([consultations](2026-05-07-world-bank-ethiopia-cpf-2027-2036-public-consultations)).

The standing basis is constitutional: citizens have the right to participate in public affairs directly or through elected representatives, and government has a duty to promote participation in forming national development policies ([constitution](1995-08-21-ethiopia-constitution-proclamation-1-1995)).

The base holds participation events, not their effect: nothing records which recommendations were adopted.

summary: Two national disability inclusion guidelines were disseminated, moving from policy development to mandated implementation ([guideline](2026-02-05-ecdd-guideline-inclusion-skill-development-employment)).
developments:
The national guideline for inclusion of persons with disabilities in skill development and employment was officially disseminated in February 2026, developed with the labour and skills ministry after a one-year review and moving from policy development to implementation across technical training and the labour market ([guideline](2026-02-05-ecdd-guideline-inclusion-skill-development-employment)).

A disability inclusion guideline for food security was launched at a national dissemination workshop in August 2025 and handed over to the women and social affairs ministry, the urban and infrastructure ministry and disability associations ([workshop](2025-08-15-ecdd-disability-inclusion-guideline-food-security)).

The statutory basis is Ethiopia's ratification of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2010 ([ratification](2010-06-11-ethiopia-crpd-ratification-proclamation-676-2010)).

Neither guideline addresses digital access, and the base holds nothing on accessibility requirements for public digital services.

2026-09-01 — an operator foundation and the national federation of disability associations signed a three-year memorandum framing collaboration on digital inclusion, accessible technology, inclusive education, economic empowerment, healthcare and rights advocacy ([memorandum](2026-09-01-techafricanews-safaricom-ethiopia-feapd-disability)). It is the first private-sector instrument on this indicator; the two guidelines before it were state ones, and no target, budget or beneficiary count is attached to any of the three.

progress: No change, a first measurement of the sole exchange with no earlier figure behind it
summary: The country's only internet exchange carries three members and 21 Gbps of cumulative port capacity ([tracker](2026-01-01-internet-society-pulse-ixp-tracker-addix)).
developments:
Measurement from self-reported peering data, last updated in January 2026, records the Addis Ababa Internet Exchange with three members, 21 Gbps of cumulative port speeds, all three members peering at the route server and two of the three using route origin validation ([tracker](2026-01-01-internet-society-pulse-ixp-tracker-addix)).

The exchange, the country's first, had by September 2025 been operating for over a year at a Tier III data centre in the technology park ([update](2025-09-04-wingu-africa-transforming-connectivity-addix-ixp)).

The base holds no earlier capacity or membership figure, so the level is stated and the direction is not. It holds no second exchange and none outside the capital.

progress: Mixed, service prices rose sharply at the second operator while a device-affordability pilot was extended to Ethiopia
summary: The second operator raised data prices by 20 to 82 percent from December 2025 ([report](2025-12-28-safaricom-ethiopia-data-price-hike)) while a US$40 smartphone pilot named Ethiopia ([pilot](2026-03-03-gsma-affordable-40-smartphones-pilot-africa)).
developments:
Safaricom Ethiopia revised its data packages from 23 December 2025, raising prices by between 20 and 82 percent across most plans while cutting data volumes on several: the weekly 10GB bundle at 250 birr was reduced to 5.5GB, and the 100 birr weekly package to 2GB from 3GB ([report](2025-12-28-safaricom-ethiopia-data-price-hike)). The operator cited operational and investment costs, the birr devaluation and prior below-cost pricing.

Ethiopia was named one of six African countries for a 2026 pilot of entry-level 4G smartphones in the US$30-40 range by the handset affordability coalition ([pilot](2026-03-03-gsma-affordable-40-smartphones-pilot-africa)).

The most recent market assessment is from July 2025 ([assessment](2025-07-01-ethiopia-telecom-market-assessment-world-bank)); its affordability figures are not in the captured text, so the base holds no price-to-income measure against which to size the increase.

progress: Advanced, on commercial capacity rather than on any government continuity plan
summary: Off-site capacity grew with a new private cloud platform and Tier III expansion, while the government's own assessed absence of a continuity plan stands ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)).
developments:
Wingu Cloud Exchange launched in March 2026, a locally hosted private cloud platform offering compute, storage, container management and security, expanding in-country off-site storage and data-residency options ([launch](2026-03-31-wingu-africa-launches-wingu-cloud-exchange-ethiopia)).

Ethio telecom's annual performance report for the year to June 2026 reports network and data-centre capacity expansion under its 2028 strategy, including Tier III facilities ([annual report](2026-07-23-ethiotelecom-annual-business-performance-report-2025-26)); the capacity figures are not in the captured text.

The government's own 2023 assessment found neither a business continuity plan nor a disaster recovery plan in place and recommended a framework with prioritised recovery sites ([assessment](2023-02-01-mint-assessment-provision-e-government-services)).

Nothing since states that such a plan was adopted, so capacity has grown and the obligation to use it has not been created.

progress: Advanced, on import control and diagnosis rather than on any rule addressed to AI harms
summary: A security-clearance directive reached new and emerging technology products, and an AI readiness assessment was used to identify governance gaps ([directive](2026-05-01-insa-it-products-security-clearance-directive-1135-2026)).
developments:
Directive 1135/2026 creates security clearance, permit and monitoring procedures for restricted and prohibited information technology products and provides for designating new or emerging products ([directive](2026-05-01-insa-it-products-security-clearance-directive-1135-2026)).

UNESCO reported that a creative-industries forum in Addis Ababa in June 2026 surfaced findings from Ethiopia's AI readiness assessment, used to identify governance gaps and reform priorities for responsible artificial intelligence ([report](2026-07-02-unesco-dialogue-ethical-ai-culture-youth-leadership)).

The governing instrument remains the 2024 National Artificial Intelligence Policy, a Council of Ministers policy rather than binding law ([policy](2024-06-01-ethiopia-national-artificial-intelligence-policy)).

The base holds no rule on automated decision-making, no complaint or redress route for an AI-caused harm, and no enforcement action.

summary: Artificial intelligence entered sectoral systems in agriculture, health and cross-government monitoring ([platform](2026-05-18-ethiopia-data-sovereignty-ai-monitoring-platform)).
developments:
A national conference reported a unified digital monitoring and evaluation platform across more than 113 public institutions, with an AI-powered survey dashboard ([platform](2026-05-18-ethiopia-data-sovereignty-ai-monitoring-platform)).

Ethiopia OpenAgriNet launched in February 2026, an AI-powered agricultural platform built on open standards with consent-based data governance, developed by the Agricultural Transformation Institute with partners ([launch](2026-02-03-ethiopia-openagrinet-launch)).

The research institute and the health ministry completed training on AI-PRESCRIBER, a clinical decision support system, with specialists from 13 hospitals each delegating one expert ([training](2026-03-06-ahri-moh-ai-prescriber-training)).

These are launches and trainings. The base holds no usage figure, no accuracy or safety evaluation, and no statement that any of them has changed a sectoral decision.
